Two scheduled rows carry the assistant's work on its own library: **25 stages**, of which 7 call a model. Capture runs in minutes; consolidation runs once a day, and its cron is the only thing ordering any of them. Everything else that runs unasked — including the upkeep of the machine itself — is on the [What runs on its own](/reference/what-runs/) page.

> These are the **shipped defaults**. What you can change lives in a
> config file you own once TESSERACT is installed, so your copy may
> differ, and should, once you tune it.


## `capture` — every 5 minutes

Seals what the last few minutes produced into memory leaves, and recaps any conversation that has gone quiet.

**Without it:** Turns and terminal work would wait for the nightly pass, anything the machine lost before it would never be captured at all, and a conversation held anywhere would leave nothing behind, so the next one would start from nothing.

| 1 | `leaf_intake` | Admits waiting leaves and appends them to their buffer. | — | continuous | 2 min |
| 2 | `leaf_seal` | Compresses a buffer that crossed its size or age threshold into one seal, and marks its leaves sealed. | `leaf_intake` | continuous | 2 min |
| 3 | `conversation_reflect` | Writes one recap for every conversation that has gone quiet, whichever entry point it arrived through, tagged with that entry point. | `leaf_seal` | continuous | 2 min |

## `consolidate` — 17:00 every day

Settles the day into the library: digest, distil, lint, scrub, re-index. It sweeps the agenda and the providers on the way.

**Without it:** The library would grow by accretion: duplicates never merged, broken links never repaired, indexes drifting from the files they describe.

It consumes `leaf_seals` from the other row — declared, so nothing reads across rows by accident.

| # | Stage | What it does | Runs after | Due | Budget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `agenda_reap` | Abandons the items on the agenda that have sat unfinished past their horizon, so a backlog nobody can finish never crowds out new work. | — | daily | 1 min |
| 2 | `conscience_heartbeat` | Scrapes the day's failures, idle jobs and open breakers into a drift report. | — | daily | 2 min |
| 3 | `daily_writer` | Rolls the day's scheduled runs into the daily log layer. | — | daily | 2 min |
| 4 | `leaf_digest_daily` | Recomputes one digest across every seal written that day. | `leaf_seal`† | daily | 5 min |
| 5 | `leaf_topic_route` | Files each seal's sections under the topics its entities earned. | `leaf_seal`† | daily | 5 min |
| 6 | `vault_raw_watch` | Ingests what you dropped in the vault's raw folder; anything that fails a safety filter is held for you. | — | daily | 15 min |
| 7 | `vault_lint` | Checks the vault wiki for orphans, stale pages, contradictions and missing hubs. | `vault_raw_watch` | daily | 10 min |
| 8 | `work_index_sweep` | Drops index rows pointing at sessions and files that no longer exist. | — | daily | 3 min |
| 9 | `chat_digest` (model) | Reads yesterday's conversations and writes down what mattered. | — | daily | 10 min |
| 10 | `retention` | Ages everything the retention table names — old sessions to the archive, spent logs away, and the permission ledger's old rows to a dated file beside it. | `chat_digest` | daily | 5 min |
| 11 | `feedback_consolidator` (model) | Reviews the whole active feedback set and proposes merges — also as proposals only. | — | weekly | 10 min |
| 12 | `feedback_sweep` (model) | Looks for standing instructions you gave in passing and proposes them; it never writes one itself. | — | daily | 10 min |
| 13 | `librarian_heartbeat` (model) | Consolidates the raw daily layer into canonical memory and refreshes the index. | `chat_digest` | daily | 10 min |
| 14 | `dream_cycle` | Promotes what you keep recalling into longer-lived memory. | `librarian_heartbeat` | daily | 10 min |
| 15 | `memory_lint` | Scans the memory store for broken links, stale paths and empty stubs. | `dream_cycle`, `librarian_heartbeat` | daily | 5 min |
| 16 | `memory_scrub` | Repairs the findings it safely can, and leaves the ones needing your decision. | `memory_lint`\* | daily | 5 min |
| 17 | `index_rebuild` | Rebuilds the keyword and vector indexes over the settled store. | `memory_scrub` | daily | 15 min |
| 18 | `atlas_build` | Redraws the map of how everything you have saved connects — memories, wiki pages, sources and the names in them. | `index_rebuild`, `memory_scrub` | daily | 10 min |
| 19 | `atlas_verify` | Weekly. Redraws the map a second time and checks it matches the one on disk, so the map can never quietly become the thing it describes. | `atlas_build`\* | weekly | 10 min |
| 20 | `memory_relink` (model) | Looks up the memories the map says nothing connects to, and tries to find them relatives. | `atlas_build`\*, `atlas_verify` | daily | 10 min |
| 21 | `provider_probe` (model) | Sends one known-good call to every model you have configured, the backups included, so a dead key or a retired model is found here rather than in the middle of your next request. | — | daily | 10 min |
| 22 | `brief_render` (model) | Writes tomorrow morning's brief, last, so it knows what the night actually did — delivery is a separate service that sends it at the hour you set. | `memory_relink`, `provider_probe`, `retention` | daily | 10 min |

## Order is declared, not timed

A stage names what must run before it, and the runner derives the order above from those names — it is not the order they are written in. Three kinds of edge, and the difference matters when something breaks: a **data** dependency (marked \* in the table) means the stage consumes what the other one produced, so it is skipped when that one did not succeed. A plain ordering edge only places it later; the stage still runs. And † marks a stage waiting on the OTHER row's output — the two rows fire apart, so it reads what the last capture left rather than waiting for one.

That distinction is why an unreachable model cannot cost you the day's maintenance. The deterministic stages commit before anything waits on a provider, and nothing downstream of a model stage is skipped unless it actually reads what that stage writes.

The daily row's own cadence — `0 17 * * *`, 17:00 every day — is the only clock in the whole arrangement. Move that one line and every stage moves with it, keeping its order.

## Missing a day costs one run, not the work

Each stage remembers how far it got. Come back after a week away and a stage is handed the whole week as one window rather than being run seven times — and the few stages that can only think in single days walk the days they missed, oldest first, bounded so a month away cannot become a month of model calls in one run.

## What a stage reports

Every stage says what came of it, plus how much it changed and how much it declined to touch. There is no state for *ran, produced nothing, called it a win*.

| Outcome | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `succeeded` | It ran and produced something. |
| `skipped_no_work` | It ran and there was nothing to do. Healthy, and it says so rather than reporting a success. |
| `refused` | It deliberately did not start — you turned it off, a breaker was open, or something it needs was missing. |
| `degraded` | It produced less than it promises. A rebuild without embeddings is the usual one. |
| `truncated` | It ran out of its time budget; the rest resumes next run from where it stopped. |
| `failed` | It tried and errored. |
| `caller_error` | It worked, and it was asked for something it cannot do: a file that is not there, a setting of the wrong shape, work that was already finished. Being asked wrong is not the same as being broken, so it is counted separately. |
| `unverified` | It acted, nothing went wrong, and it left no mark anyone can go and check. Neither a success nor a failure, and it is counted in its own column rather than folded into either. |
| `skipped_upstream_failed` | Something it consumes did not succeed, so running it would work from stale input. |
